extracted.intended_audience: aspiring fiction writers (short stories, novels, comics) and storytellers learning craft
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on writing fiction and storytelling across forms (short fiction, novels, comics), emphasizing voice, plotting, description, worldbuilding, revision practice, and ethical responsibilities. Practical lessons cover craft techniques, process habits, and evaluative principles for producing engaging stories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the lie of a made-up story to tell a human truth
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the central tools of literature is using the lie of a made-up story to tell a human truth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fiction's authority comes from this paradox — the invented serves the true. Stories should aim to reveal human truths via fabricated events and characters; evaluate whether the story's invention conveys an honest emotional or moral insight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Developing your voice
rubrics_metrics.description: What makes a paragraph recognizable as yours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Voice is distinctiveness at the sentence/paragraph level. Look for consistent choices in rhythm, diction, point of view, and attitude that make prose unmistakably the author's. Cultivate voice by practice and by allowing personal quirks to surface.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overcoming fear of mistakes
rubrics_metrics.description: Permission to fail in early drafts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: During drafting, prioritize getting material down rather than perfecting sentences. Accepting mistakes enables discovery; reserve judgment and heavy editing for revision phases.

rubrics_metrics.name: The compost heap (gathering material)
rubrics_metrics.description: Accumulate experiences, observations, fragments; let them decay into usable matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect bits of life, overheard phrases, ideas, and moments. Allow time and subconscious processing to turn raw material into story-ready elements. Evaluate stories by how well they recycle and transform lived detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Old stories from new angles
rubrics_metrics.description: Every story has been told; what is new is the angle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Freshness comes from perspective, voice, or the combination of elements rather than absolute novelty. Judge originality by the angle or framing applied to familiar material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cold opens
rubrics_metrics.description: Start before the reader is oriented; orient them through action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open scenes with momentum/curiosity rather than exposition. A strong opening throws the reader into immediate stakes and orients via character action and sensory detail instead of info-dumps. Assess openings on whether they create urgent questions and quickly establish voice or tone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withholding information
rubrics_metrics.description: Strategic omission creates engagement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Don't tell everything at once; withhold selectively to sustain curiosity and allow readers to infer. Avoid withholding that becomes confusing rather than intriguing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emotional weight in details
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose details that carry feeling, not just data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select specifics that resonate emotionally or reveal character. Prefer details that do narrative or emotional work over neutral description. Evaluate scenes on whether their details deepen feeling or simply fill space.

rubrics_metrics.name: Memorable details
rubrics_metrics.description: One specific over many general.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A single vivid, concrete detail often outperforms pages of abstract description. Use striking specifics to anchor scenes and memory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Realistic dialogue
rubrics_metrics.description: Listen to people; trust your characters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dialogue should reflect believable speech rhythms while serving character and scene. Avoid on-the-nose exposition; let subtext, interruptions, and small gestures carry meaning. Test dialogue by reading aloud and trusting what characters would actually say.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characters in unfamiliar situations
rubrics_metrics.description: Pressure that creates tension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Put characters into strange or difficult circumstances to reveal choices and character. Tension arises from character reactions to novelty or stress rather than contrived plot devices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Listen to your characters
rubrics_metrics.description: They will tell you what they want to do.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow characters' impulses to guide plot decisions; character-led plotting feels organic. If characters behave implausibly, re-evaluate characterization rather than forcing plot.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make the world feel real
rubrics_metrics.description: Through specific consequences, not exhaustive description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show how the world affects people and plot; demonstrate consequences of rules or changes. Economical worldbuilding grounded in character and cause-and-effect is preferable to broad lore dumps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid common worldbuilding pitfalls
rubrics_metrics.description: Over-explanation, lore-dumping.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resist explaining every rule or history; reveal necessary world details through scenes and character needs. Assess whether worldbuilding supports the story's stakes rather than overwhelming it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Know your genre
rubrics_metrics.description: Its conventions are your contract with the reader.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize reader expectations tied to genre and either satisfy them or intentionally subvert with awareness. Evaluate work on genre-fitness: does it deliver (or knowingly challenge) the experiences readers anticipate?

rubrics_metrics.name: Humor as a craft tool
rubrics_metrics.description: Including 'sherbert lemons' and 'figgins' — small unexpected delights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Humor is not optional; it can carry emotional weight and relieve tension. Use small, unexpected pleasures and named techniques to surprise readers. Judge humor on its timing, appropriateness, and contribution to tone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't rewrite while drafting
rubrics_metrics.description: Write the whole thing through; revise later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separate creation from editing. Complete a draft to discover structure and content, then revise in subsequent passes. Avoid polishing line-level prose prematurely if it blocks forward progress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Whittle in revision
rubrics_metrics.description: Finished draft → strip away.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revision is often subtraction: remove excess, tighten, and clarify. Look for redundancies, dead weight, and opportunities to intensify through omission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Daily devotion
rubrics_metrics.description: Show up every day.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practice consistently; regular writing habits build craft and produce material. Evaluate productivity and improvement by consistency, not inspiration alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods for getting unstuck
rubrics_metrics.description: Switch projects, walk, change format, work on something else.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use practical tactics to overcome writer's block rather than waiting. Changing viewpoint or medium can unlock progress; assess whether such methods lead to renewed momentum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plot and script structure for visual storytelling
rubrics_metrics.description: Structure guidance specific to comics and graphic novels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider beats, pacing, and division of information between text and image. Structure should account for page turns, panels, and the reader's visual processing; scripts must convey timing and visual emphasis even if the writer can't draw.

rubrics_metrics.name: You don't need to draw to write comics
rubrics_metrics.description: Emphasis that writers can craft comics without being illustrators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on clear visual storytelling, scene construction, and collaboration with artists. Evaluate comic scripts on clarity of visual intent, not artistic rendering.

rubrics_metrics.name: The artist's responsibility to audience
rubrics_metrics.description: Consideration of what the storyteller owes readers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be mindful of ethical and emotional impacts of stories; think about representation, consequences, and the effects on readers. Judge work on whether it treats subjects and audiences with responsibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: What stories do to and for human beings
rubrics_metrics.description: Reflection on story function and effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess stories for their social, psychological, or moral functions: solace, challenge, explanation, or provocation. Evaluate whether the story's effect aligns with its intentions and ethical stance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trust the unfamiliar
rubrics_metrics.description: Strange situations open character.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Embrace the odd or uncanny as a tool to reveal character and theme. Avoid sanitizing strangeness; instead, use it to test and expose characters' interiority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specifics over abstractions
rubrics_metrics.description: One true detail outweighs paragraphs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor concrete, sensory particulars that make scenes vivid rather than abstract exposition. Use specifics to ground emotion and theme.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genre as contract
rubrics_metrics.description: Meet (or knowingly violate) reader expectation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be intentional about fulfilling or subverting genre conventions; unexpected violations should be signaled or motivated, not accidental. Evaluate whether deviations serve the story or confuse readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Humor should be load-bearing
rubrics_metrics.description: Humor is not optional; it can carry structural or thematic weight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use humor to advance plot, reveal character, or modulate tone. Check if comedic elements support the story rather than merely decorating it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Daily writing as discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: Talent without practice produces nothing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regular practice is essential to craft development. Measure progress by accumulated practice and revision cycles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinctiveness of voice (evaluative)
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the writing feel recognizably individual?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate submissions on whether voice makes the work stand out and carries the narrative. Look for consistent choices in syntax, imagery, and perspective that form an authorial signature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specificity vs. generality of detail (evaluative)
rubrics_metrics.description: Are details specific and emotionally resonant rather than vague and abstract?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer scenes with concrete, memorable details that do narrative work. Penalize florid abstraction that fails to reveal character or advance story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strength of opening (evaluative)
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the story open with a compelling incitement or cold open that orients via action?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess openings for immediate stakes, curiosity, and voice. Weak openings over-explain or delay engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character-led plotting (evaluative)
rubrics_metrics.description: Do events flow from who the characters are rather than arbitrary plot needs?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge plots on whether character desires and flaws plausibly drive choices and outcomes. Avoid plots that require characters to act inconsistently just to produce events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Worldbuilding economy (evaluative)
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the world feel real through consequences rather than exposition?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Score worldbuilding on whether it emerges naturally from scenes and affects character choices. Penalize excessive lore that doesn't influence plot or stakes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Honesty of the truth being told via the lie (evaluative)
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the fictional lie reveal or illuminate a believable human truth?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the story's invented elements convincingly communicate emotional or thematic truth, rather than relying on gimmick or shock alone.
